record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: How is turbulent energy distributed in space and time in kinetic plasma turbulence? The question concerns the spatio-temporal organization of turbulent energy, rather than only its scale-by-scale spectrum, and is posed as a fundamental target for future multi-spacecraft measurements.

evidence.quote: This includes answering fundamental questions about, for instance, (i) the distribution of turbulent energy in space and time

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a collisionless or weakly collisional magnetized plasma whose dynamics are governed by the Vlasov–Maxwell system

  ∂_t f_s + v·∇_x f_s + (q_s/m_s)(E + v×B/c)·∇_v f_s = 0,    s ∈ {ions, electrons},
  ∇×B = (4π/c) J + (1/c) ∂_t E,    ∇×E = −(1/c) ∂_t B,
  ∇·E = 4π ρ,    ∇·B = 0,

with current and charge densities J = Σ_s q_s ∫ v f_s dv and ρ = Σ_s q_s ∫ f_s dv. Suppose the system is driven into a statistically stationary, fully developed turbulent state on a triply periodic three-dimensional spatial domain with three-dimensional velocity space (3D3V), with a mean magnetic field B_0 and turbulent fluctuations spanning scales from the magnetohydrodynamic range through the ion and electron kinetic ranges.

Define the local fluctuation energy density

  ε(x,t) = (|δB(x,t)|² + |δE(x,t)|²)/(8π) + Σ_s ∫ (m_s |v − u_s|² / 2) δf_s(x,v,t) dv,

and its space–time correlation/spectral structure via the four-dimensional Fourier transform ε̂(k,ω) of ε(x,t) (or, equivalently, of the underlying electromagnetic and particle-fluctuation fields).

Problem. Characterize quantitatively how turbulent energy is distributed jointly in physical space x and in time t (equivalently, in wavenumber k and frequency ω) in such a kinetic plasma turbulence state. In particular:

(a) Determine the joint (k,ω) energy distribution across the inertial, ion-kinetic, and electron-kinetic ranges, identifying which fraction of energy lies on linear wave dispersion surfaces ω = ω_α(k) (e.g. Alfvén, slow, kinetic Alfvén, whistler, ion-cyclotron branches) versus in non-wavelike, advected or coherent structures.

(b) Quantify the degree of spatial intermittency (volume-filling factor, multifractal scaling exponents of structure functions, and statistics of energy-dissipation surrogates) and the temporal intermittency (waiting-time and burst-duration distributions) of the energy density ε(x,t).

(c) Provide a predictive theory linking (a) and (b) to the driving parameters (plasma beta, ion-to-electron mass and temperature ratios, Alfvén Mach number, system size in units of ρ_i and d_i).

Give either a rigorous derivation, a closed phenomenological model with verified scaling laws, or a definitive numerical/observational characterization.
artifact.status_search_result: The spatio-temporal distribution of energy in kinetic plasma turbulence remains an active open research target. Recent reviews and mission-science papers (e.g., HelioSwarm, MMS multi-spacecraft analyses) explicitly list disentangling the joint (k,ω) energy distribution and characterizing intermittent spatial/temporal structure as outstanding goals not yet resolved by theory, simulation, or observation.

status_evidence.title: HelioSwarm mission concept
status_evidence.snippet: HelioSwarm will measure plasma turbulence simultaneously at multiple points and scales to reveal how energy is distributed across space and time.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the spatio-temporal energy distribution in space plasma turbulence is a stated, unresolved scientific objective.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions include the distribution of turbulent energy in space and time.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as an open fundamental question for kinetic plasma turbulence.
